Subject: POC trial planning: workload & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC moving:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: patient intake triage + summarization for AcmeHealth telemedicine flows.
- Main success criteria (customer-defined):
  1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for 256-token responses.
  2) Cost: < $0.01 per completed query (token-adjusted).
  3) Accuracy: >= 90% match on entity extraction & triage label against your internal gold set.
  4) Stability: No more than 0.5% failed requests under normal traffic.

Workload & traffic profile (need confirmation)
- Baseline RPS: 8 rps average during business hours (PST).
- Peak concurrency: 40 concurrent requests during daily bursts.
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens average; typical response: 200-300 tokens.
- Burst patterns: 10-15 minute spikes in mornings (08:00-09:00) and after 17:00.

Proposed POC plan (attached PDF)
- 2-week technical validation + 4-week extended trial for performance/cost tuning.
- Deliverables: workload replay harness, performance report, cost estimates, and a quality eval run against your gold prompts.
- Ownership: Redwood (Ben + Marissa) to run infra and onboarding; AcmeHealth to provide gold set + test endpoints.

Next steps
1) Alex: confirm workload numbers above and share the workload_profile.xlsx with exact RPS histograms and sample prompts (we'll use these for replay).
2) Ben/Marissa: turn around a finalized POC schedule and access checklist within 48 hours of receiving the profile.
3) Align on security requirements (SOC2 evidence, VPC needs) - loop in your procurement/security contact.

Attachments: redwood_poc_plan.pdf (POC timeline & responsibilities).

If that looks good I'll lock in target kickoff for Mon Jul 5.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: POC trial planning: workload & success criteria - AcmeHealth

Thanks Ben - appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and the workload file attached.

Confirmed success criteria look right. A couple notes:
- Latency: 95th <= 350ms is a stretch but acceptable as target for the POC. If we see systematic tail issues we may loosen to 400ms for the extended trial.
- Cost: we want a first-pass estimate by model/quantization options.

Workload (see attached acme_workload_profile.xlsx):
- Avg RPS: 7.5 (09:00-17:00 PST window).
- Sustained concurrency: 12-18 typical; peak concurrency observed: 52 (five-minute window) during Monday morning spikes.
- Request token lengths: prompt avg 110 tokens (sigma ~40); response avg 260 tokens (sigma ~100). Max payloads we've seen up to ~1200 tokens in edge cases.
- Burst pattern: short high spikes (~2-5 minutes) every 30-45 minutes during business hours; larger morning spike ~20 minutes.

Attached: acme_workload_profile.xlsx (contains histograms + sample prompts)

Security: procurement included in CC - they will send standard NDA/POC SOW redlines separately. We are SOC2 Type II compliant internally and will share the evidence if needed.

I'll be out Thu-Fri next week but Jul 5 kickoff still works for our team.

Best,
Alex

AcmeHealth

Alex - thanks for the workload file and the detail, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups: 

1) Peak concurrency 52 in five minutes - noted. We'll plan the initial infra to handle 60 concurrent workers for safety and run a capacity test during week 1.
2) Token max ~1200: we'll configure streaming and chunking options for those edge cases; also propose a fallback policy to a smaller model for very long payloads if latency SLAs are violated.
3) For cost estimates we'll run two profiles: fp16 on A100s (baseline) and an int8-quantized variant on T4s (cost-optimized). Expect estimates in 24-48 hours.

Action owners:
- Redwood: Marissa -> infra setup & capacity test; Dylan -> replay harness + performance scripts; Ben -> commercial SOW/POC cadence.
- AcmeHealth: Alex -> sample gold set + procurement redlines.

I'll drop a proposed kickoff agenda and timeline in the shared Drive link shortly.
